newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - June U.S. T-bonds seen circling 110-area.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - June U.S. T-bonds seen circling 110-area.

text.p: June U.S. Treasury bond futures, which have been hovering around the 200-day moving average in the 110-area for about a week, are likely to continue churning in that region for a while, analysts said.
While recent development had been positive, overbought daily momentum indicators needed to be corrected, they added.

"The last seven or eight trading days, the market has basically been oscillating around the 200-day moving average," said Terence Gabriel, a technical analyst at I.D.E.A. Inc. "I would expect that to continue until the market has worked off enough of the daily overbought conditions."
June T-bonds stood at 110-5/32 in late morning trade, down 7/32 on the day, after touching a fresh 2-1/2 month high of 110-22/32 early and then dropping to a low of 109-30/32.
The 200-day average came in today at 110-3/32, with the 50 percent retracement of the February-April decline also at around that level, analysts said.

Dan Busiel, a vice president at First Chicago Futures, said the fact that June T-bonds made new highs again today was positive but the outlook would turn bearish if the contract closed below the 110-00 to 110-3/32 area.

"That is going to look start looking much more negative, especially considering all the momentum indicators are turning down," he said. "If we get an outside day (by dipping below Monday's 109-28/32 low), that just adds to it."
Analysts noted that the daily stochastic and relative strength index have been in overbought territory since just after the late April breakout rally.
"We had that minor correction last week...but we bounced up so quickly that we didn't really correct the overbought conditions," Gabriel at I.D.E.A. said.

He said rallies were likely to fall short of a trendline drawn from the December highs, which today was at 111-10/32 and was declining by about 2/32 a day, or perhaps 110-30/32, the 61.8-percent retracement of the February-April decline.
But he added the market would likely find bids on weakness toward 109-7/32, the 38.2 retracement of February-April decline, or the recent low at 108-30/32.

In Eurodollar futures, the 200-day moving average was also a pivotal level for the December contract, Gabriel said. December Euros stood at 93.725, off one basis point on the day, after briefly rising earlier to the 200-day average at 93.770.
"Each time we're touching it, we're backing away," he said, referring to a minor poke above the average on May 2 and close brushes last Friday and Monday.
If the market could close above the 200-day average, it would eventually test the trendline from the December highs, coming in today at 93.98, Gabriel said.
